whatIsTrue:
Confirmed. Each claim holds as stated. Two small corrections and two extensions:

1. connected=True is set at paper_trader.py:258 (the finding says ~254). Ticks are processed even earlier, from the tick-by-tick subscription on.

2. The refusal reason depends on the broker. Against real IBKR, which lists the algo's own just-placed order in reqAllOpenOrders, start-up refuses at line 505: "an order for TQQQ is still open at IBKR. Cancel it...". That points Alex at the algo's own order as if it were a stray one. The 514 mismatch refusal appears only if the order is not listed. If the order fills before the check, the refusal reads "account holds -200 ... record says 0". In every case no cancel is sent and the order stays at IBKR.

3. The window runs from the tick-by-tick subscription to line 514: about 1.0 s (the sleep at 478 plus the open-order round trip), plus about 0.5 s more when Auto-Hedge has a record. An order can come from:
   - the stop-loss, take-profit or exit rule, which needs a minute boundary inside the window;
   - the trailing stop, which fires on the very first tick when a trailing % is set and the price is already past it. That is deterministic.

   Nothing on the timer has run yet, so the Stop button, safe mode, the position check and the backup-stop logic are not in force.

4. Extension: even with a correct record (account = record), the race makes start-up refuse on its own order. The sell is left at IBKR unsupervised: no 60 s cancel, no follow-up. The live algo is off, and the Go Live service restarts the paper trader. That is harmless only if the sell fills before the open-order listing.

The Webull algo is not affected. Its connect_api runs all checks (check_matches_broker at webull paper_trader.py:226) before streaming starts, and cancel_working sits in main's finally.
trigger:
Needs live mode on the IBKR algo, a live record that holds a position, and the price already past that position's stop-loss, take-profit, exit rule or trailing stop at the moment live trading starts. Starts happen on the Go Live button, a Mac restart with "start again after a Mac restart" on, or ./jb live.
- Chance per such start: about 2% (a minute boundary inside the roughly 1-1.5 s window). If a trailing stop % is set on the Trading options and the price is beyond it, it happens on every such start.
- The worst outcome, an unintended short, also needs the account to no longer hold the shares the record says it does: sold by hand in the IBKR app, or the backup stop filled while the algo was off. That is exactly the case the start-up check exists to catch.
- Now (both algos paper): cannot happen. Paper mode has no broker object and sends no orders.
- After Go Live: rare in a normal week, because live starts are infrequent. But each start after a price drop with a stale or held position is exposed, and with a trailing stop configured it is certain.
severityWhy: This can leave a wrong position with nothing watching it. Reproduced end to end, the result was the account short 200 TQQQ (a 3x ETF, on margin), with the live algo refused and off, no stop-loss, no backup stop, and the paper trader restarted in its place. In the no-fill case, a real sell order is left working at IBKR with no supervision. The start-up safety check that should prevent exactly this is bypassed. The chance per start is low, except when a trailing stop is set.
plainTitle: Starting live IBKR trading can send a sell before its checks, then abandon it
plainWhat: When the IBKR algo starts in live mode, it starts reading prices about a second before it checks your account. If its stop-loss or trailing stop fires in that second, it sends a real sell order. If the account check then fails, the algo quits without cancelling that order. That can leave you short shares you didn't hold, or with an order nobody is watching. This only matters once you switch to live; paper mode never sends orders.
fix: In paper_trader.run(), don't let core send orders until the start-up checks pass: add a core.ready flag, set it after check_matches_broker, and make _live/_enter refuse while it is not set. Also wrap the post-connect start-up checks in try/except SystemExit that calls self.broker.cancel_working(), waits about 1 s, then re-raises.
fixRisk:
- Ticks should still update last_price and bars while gated; only orders should wait.
- Test that a position already past its stop sells right after the checks pass, not never.
- subscribe() is shared with _reconnect_loop: the flag must stay set after the first successful start so reconnects are not blocked.
- The cancel-on-refusal must cancel only this run's own orders (broker.working) and must go out before the process exits.
- Re-run tests/algo-stress-test.py and the live-run harness.

whatIsTrue:
The mechanism is real and the line numbers are accurate. In live mode, prices are processed and orders can be sent from the moment subscribe() starts streaming. Nothing waits for the open-order and position checks. When start-up then refuses, its own order is never cancelled.

The finding overstates how reachable this is.
(1) In the scenario it describes (Mac off or trader crashed while holding, then Alex sells by SELL ALL or in the app), the algo normally still has its backup-stop record. Its exit then waits for the backup stop, so nothing is sent. Start-up books the missing shares as a backup-stop fill and carries on (v2).
(2) Only start-ups with NO backup-stop record are exposed. That happens when broker_stop_pct is 0, when the stop was refused, or when it was cancelled outside the algo and not yet re-placed: the 5-minute retry, safe mode, kill or a pending order all block re-placing. A typical path: Alex cancels the stop and sells in the IBKR app, the algo goes into safe mode, then he presses Stop Live and Go Live.
(3) An exit must be true in the start-up window: stop-loss or take-profit on a bar that closes in it, an exit rule (overnight_gap's 'clock_session == 3' is true on every regular-hours bar), or a trailing stop (any tick).
(4) Ticks must actually be used in the window. With tick-by-tick granted, a minute boundary must fall inside the ~1-2 s window (roughly 2-5% of starts), or about 100% with a trailing stop past its level. If IBKR refuses the algo's tick-by-tick, the first 3 s of ticks are dropped. That is likely, because the board's IBKR bridge holds the 3 per-user subscriptions. The race then needs a start-up longer than 3 s (slow open-order reply, Auto-Hedge lookups).

A second outcome also holds when the record matches the broker: a legitimate exit sent during start-up makes start-up refuse on its own order and leaves it working (v3). Paper mode is unaffected: no real orders and no broker check.
trigger: Live only (Go Live, ./jb live, or start-after-Mac-restart with autostart on). The algo starts while its live record shows a position and there is no logs/broker_stop.json. Inside the start-up window, an exit condition is true: stop-loss or take-profit on a closing bar, an exit rule, or a trailing stop. And the algo either gets tick-by-tick data or its start-up takes longer than 3 s. Now (both algos paper): never. After Go Live: rare. It needs the hand-sale-plus-restart kind of sequence and then a few-percent timing chance, but close to certain if a trailing stop is on and tick-by-tick is granted. In a normal week it most likely never happens.
severityWhy: When it happens the damage is CRITICAL-class: an unintended short, or an extra sale, of a 3x ETF is left working at IBKR. Nothing cancels it and no algo is running. The refusal Alex sees ('your account holds 0 shares') is no longer true, and there is no push if he pressed Go Live less than 5 minutes earlier. But the natural scenario in the finding is blocked by the backup-stop record, and the default setup probably drops ticks for the first 3 s. That leaves a narrow, live-only combination with zero exposure today, so HIGH rather than CRITICAL. The fix is small and worth doing before Go Live.
plainTitle: Live IBKR algo can sell during its start-up checks, then quit without cancelling
plainWhat: When you start live IBKR trading, the algo starts watching prices before it has checked your account. If a sell rule fires in those first one to three seconds, it can send a real sell, then stop because the check fails, and leave that sell working. If you had already sold those shares yourself, that would leave you short. It only happens in live mode, and only in an unusual case: you closed the position yourself and the algo's backup stop was also gone. It cannot happen today while both algos are on paper.
fix: In ibkr-algo/algo/paper_trader.py run(), set a 'starting' flag that _live/_exit/_trail honour (block, or queue for after the checks) until check_matches_broker has passed. Also wrap the start-up checks in try/except SystemExit that calls self.broker.cancel_working() (and waits ~1 s) before re-raising.
fixRisk: Exits that are blocked during start-up must be re-evaluated right after the checks pass. Otherwise a real stop-loss hit at start-up is skipped until the next bar. Test with the fake gateway: start-up refusal, start-up that passes with a stop already hit, the backup-stop wait path (_bstop_wait_exit), the trailing stop, and the reconnect path (_reconnect_loop calls subscribe() and must not be blocked by the start-up flag).

whatIsTrue:
The finding is correct. While a live IBKR start-up is still running its checks, the algo already acts on prices. A minute bar that closes in that gap can send a real exit order. If start-up then refuses, the process exits without cancelling the order, and IBKR keeps it working. I confirmed this end to end.

Details the original finding leaves out:
1. It also happens when the record matches the account (V4). The algo then sees its own just-sent sell as "an order still open at IBKR", refuses to start, and leaves that sell working. If the sell fills, the record still says 200 and every later start is refused until live-reset. If Alex cancels the order as the message tells him, the position has no algo watching it and, in this case, no backup stop.
2. The immediate sell only happens when the live record has no backup stop. When a backup stop is on record (the usual state for an IBKR position), the exit first cancels the backup stop and waits, so no sell goes out in the window (V3). The backup stop's cancel is still sent, though. If start-up then refuses for a different reason (Alex's own open order for the symbol, an open Auto-Hedge order), the shares are left without the broker backup stop until the next successful start.
3. The window is about 1-2 s per start: from the price subscription to the end of the checks, longer if IBKR is slow to list orders. Overnight it is nearly closed, because overnight-venue prices are ignored for the first 3 s. Exits (stop-loss, take-profit, overnight_gap's regular-hours exit rule) can fire in the window. Entries practically cannot, because there is no history yet. A trailing stop, which is off by default, would fire on any tick.
4. The Webull algo does not have this problem.
5. The phone alert after a refused automatic start says "No live orders are being sent", which is false in this case.
severityWhy: The worst case belongs in the CRITICAL class: an unwatched short in a 3x ETF on margin, plus an alert saying no live orders are being sent. Getting there needs a 1-2 s timing coincidence and an uncommon state: no backup stop on record and a sell condition already met, plus a record/account mismatch for the short outcome. The normal IBKR state, with a backup stop on record, stops the sell from going out in the window. The more common variant (record matches) causes a confusing refusal and an unwatched but intended sale, not a wrong position. Both algos are on paper today. It should still be fixed before Go Live, because the fix is small.
plainTitle: Live IBKR algo can send a sell while starting up, then quit without cancelling it
plainWhat: When live IBKR trading starts (when you press Go Live, or when it starts again on its own after a Mac restart), the algo starts reacting to prices a second or two before it has finished checking its record against your IBKR account. A stop-loss or sell rule met in that moment can send a real sell order. If the check then fails, the algo stops but leaves that order open at IBKR. If you had already sold those shares, that order could leave you short, while the phone alert says no live orders are being sent. This is rare, and it only matters once you go live (both algos are on paper now).
fix: In ibkr-algo/algo/paper_trader.py, add a ready flag: True from the start in paper mode, set True in live mode right after check_matches_broker (before warm_up), and never reset on reconnect. In on_tickers, skip the strategy's and the hedge's ticks while it is False. Also wrap the live start-up checks in try/except SystemExit so that any refusal first calls self.broker.cancel_working().
fixRisk: Prices from the first 1-2 s of a live start are dropped (up to ~20 s if IBKR is slow listing orders). warm_up() loads history right after, so only the first minute bar changes, and that bar is already incomplete today. If the flag were reset on reconnect, or left False in paper mode, the algo would stop seeing prices and its stop-loss would go blind. Test these with the fake gateway: a live start, a paper start, and a reconnect (nightly Gateway restart). tests/algo-stress-test.py builds live IBKRTrader objects (lines ~438-1011) and may feed on_tickers directly; those tests need the flag set. Re-run the start-up with a backup stop on record to confirm it is no longer cancelled before the checks pass.

alsoNoticed.title: Live start-up records a hand sale or SELL ALL (done while the algo was off) as a backup-stop fill at the stop price
alsoNoticed.detail: ibkr-algo/algo/paper_trader.py:498-501 calls core_trader.py:686-704 bstop_filled_while_away() whenever the live record has a backup stop that IBKR no longer lists and the account holds fewer shares. It never checks whether the stop actually filled or was cancelled. SELL ALL cancels every order including the backup stop (gateway/killswitch.py:284 reqGlobalCancel) and then sells; Alex can also sell in the IBKR app. If either happens while the live algo is off, the next live start records 'filled by broker stop' at the stop price, with the note 'the backup stop at the broker sold while the algo was off'. That gives a wrong exit price in the live P&L and daily-loss figure, and a wrong explanation. CONFIRMED with /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/d5f7f21c-dc3e-504d-8a31-86f6d5f4dac4/scratchpad/verify/work/A0-impact/misbook_check.py: long 200 @ 80, stop 77.6, account 0 -> booked 'broker-stop 200 @ 77.6'. Fix: look up the stop's real outcome (completed orders by permId, or today's executions via ib.fills()) before booking. If it did not fill, book at the real fill or refuse as for any other mismatch.

whatIsTrue:
Every claim in both members is true.

1. After Alex sells the algo's shares himself in the broker app, the algo's next exit sends a closing order for the full ledger count without asking the broker. That exit can be the stop-loss, the exit rule or the trailing stop.
   - The window runs until the second mismatched position check: 60-120 s after the sale, longer while one of the algo's own orders is pending.
   - At IBKR (margin account) that sell fills as a short sale. Reproduced: account at -200 TQQQ about 55 s after the hand sale.
   - Partial hand sales give a partial short the same way.
2. Safe mode then blocks the algo's own orders, but the backup stop stays at IBKR for the full ledger count. Step 3 compares it with the ledger only, and nothing cancels or resizes it.
   - It shorts when the price goes through the backup-stop level before a minute bar closes below the algo's stop-loss: a fast drop or a gap at the 4 am / 9:30 open. Reproduced: -200.
   - It also shorts when the algo isn't acting: a session not enabled for live, or the algo stopped. On a restart the start-up adopts the stop, then refuses with "position differs" (paper_trader 487-514), so the stop stays at IBKR with nothing watching it. This part was traced.
   - In a gradual fall, the algo's own stop-loss (still checked in safe mode) cancels the stale stop first and is then blocked (the A1 path), so no short. Reproduced.
3. After the stale stop fills, the ledger books it as the algo's own "broker-stop" exit, so the P&L is wrong: the real hand sale is never booked. The push "Backup stop sold" reads as normal. The safe-mode text stays stale ("broker says 0, algo says 200") and there is no new push saying the account is short.
4. Webull (B17): the same core code sends SELL <full record> within 1-2 min; confirmed. Webull has separate SELL and SHORT order sides, so Webull most likely refuses a SELL above holdings. Then the result is one rejection followed by safe mode, with no short (traced; Webull's real answer unverifiable).
   - A Webull open sell order probably holds the shares, so Alex would likely have to cancel the backup stop before hand-selling. That makes the "stop stays old size" part unlikely at Webull.
   - The money risk is mainly at IBKR.
trigger:
Live mode only, and only when Alex sells some or all of the algo's position himself in the IBKR or Webull app while the algo is running. The board's Stop and SELL ALL buttons are handled safely.
- Double sale: an algo exit (stop-loss, exit rule or trailing stop) fires within about 1-2 min after his sale. That is likely, because people usually hand-sell into a falling price, which is when the stop-loss is about to fire.
- Stale stop: price falls or gaps through the backup-stop level (stop-loss + 1%) while safe mode lasts. Safe mode lasts until he presses Stop or runs live-reset and restarts. Overnight gaps in 3x ETFs, his main style, make the 4 am / 9:30 trigger realistic.
- Now (both algos paper): cannot happen. Paper sends no orders, places no backup stop and skips the broker position check.
- After Go Live: rare to occasional, depending on whether he manages algo positions from the broker app. When it happens on IBKR, the account is short a 3x ETF on margin.
severityWhy: At IBKR, with real ib_async and a broker that behaves like a margin account, the algo leaves the account short 200 shares of a 3x ETF. That happens through either path: the algo's own second sale, or the stale backup stop. Nothing covers the short automatically. The follow-up push either says only "positions differ" or, for the stop path, reads as a normal "Backup stop sold". This is a wrong position with real money at risk once live. Webull is likely protected by its SELL/SHORT distinction, but that is unverified.
plainTitle: If you sell the algo's shares in the broker app, the algo can sell again and leave you short
plainWhat: If you sell the algo's shares yourself in the IBKR app, the algo doesn't notice for 1-2 minutes. If its stop-loss fires in that time, it sells the same shares again, so your account ends up short. Its backup stop order also stays at IBKR for shares you no longer own, so a fast drop or a morning gap can also leave you short. Use the board's Stop or SELL ALL buttons instead; they check the account first.
fix:
1. In _live, for every closing order that isn't the kill switch: read _broker_shares() first. If it can't be read, wait and retry. If the broker holds nothing (or the opposite side), call _mark_flat and send nothing. If it holds less, cut the order to what it holds.
2. In _bstop_tick step 3, and as soon as the position check sees the broker holding less than the ledger: cancel the backup stop, or re-place it at the broker's real size.
fixRisk:
- Never treat an unreadable or empty position list as 0. The IBKR position list is empty right after a reconnect or nightly restart, and the Webull HTTP read can fail.
- IBKR position updates can lag a fill by a moment, so a cut-down sell could under-sell right after a partial fill.
- Webull adds an HTTP call per exit (rate limits).
- Retest:
  - SELL ALL and the Stop button
  - partial fills
  - the 'unknown' backup-stop branch (743-759)
  - start-up adoption of a stop
  - Auto-Hedge orders
  - tests/algo-stress-test.py for both algos

- My own test: WORKDIR/refute_a11.py (it uses a copy of the repo), output in WORKDIR/refute_a11.out.txt:

Webull (B17):
- Closing sells go out as side SELL and short entries as SHORT (webull live_broker.py:81-85; the SDK's webull/trade/common/order_side.py has BUY/SELL/SHORT).

No processes left running; no real services contacted.
whatIsTrue:
The IBKR member (A11) holds. After you sell the live algo's shares yourself, the algo keeps trading on its own record:
- **Second sell.** Any exit (stop-loss, take-profit, exit rule, trailing stop) in the 60-120 s before the second position check sends a full-size SELL. In a margin account IBKR takes it as a short sale. My test shows the exit-rule case too, e.g. overnight_gap's sell at the open firing right after you sold at 9:30.
- **Stale backup stop.** The GTC backup stop stays at IBKR for the shares you no longer hold. The algo never resizes or cancels it on a position mismatch, and safe mode stops new orders but not that stop.

One nuance makes "the stop stays" less absolute than written. If the algo's own stop-loss, take-profit or exit rule is reached first in a session turned on for live trading, the algo cancels the stale stop (through A1's path) and its sell is then blocked by safe mode. Pressing Stop also cleans up. So the stale stop actually fires, and leaves you short, in these cases:
- a drop in pre-market or after-hours while live trading is regular hours only (the default);
- a move of more than about 1% between two 1-minute bar closes;
- 4 am after an overnight drop (IBKR takes no stops overnight);
- while the algo is stopped, or refused to start because of the mismatch.

The same trigger also comes from the board itself. The order ticket, Flip, guards and scheduled or sell-at-open sells all sell whatever the account holds, including a live algo's shares. They have no idea which shares the algo owns.

The Webull member (B17) is partly wrong about what happens at the broker. The core code does the same thing, but Webull's rules very likely stop the harm:
- the algo's extra closing sell is side SELL, not SHORT, so Webull should refuse it as more than you hold rather than open a short;
- while the backup stop is resting, Webull treats it as a pending sell-to-close, so a sale by hand of those shares is refused until you cancel the stop. If you cancel it, safe mode then blocks it from being placed again, so no oversized stop is left.

This Webull part is traced from Webull help and API docs, not checked against the real Webull US.

Line numbers quoted in both members are accurate.
trigger:
The live algo must hold a position, and you sell those shares yourself (IBKR app, or the board's ticket, Flip, guard or scheduled sell).

- **Second sell:** an algo exit fires within about 1-2 minutes of your sale.
- **Stale stop:** price later falls to entry minus (stop_loss + 1)% in a window when IBKR's stop is active (4 am-8 pm) but the algo isn't acting: a session not turned on for live trading, a fast move inside one bar, 4 am after an overnight drop, or the algo down or refused at start-up. The stop is GTC, so this can happen days later while safe mode lasts.

Now, with both algos on paper: impossible. Paper mode sends no orders, has no backup stop and doesn't trade the real account.

After Go Live on IBKR: likely within weeks for a hands-on trader who overrides the algo from his phone. The stale-stop path is the more likely one, because live defaults to regular hours only while Alex trades extended hours. The 1-2 minute double-sell needs a coincidence, but a real one, for example selling yourself at the open when overnight_gap sells at 9:31.

After Go Live on Webull: mostly a refused order, if Webull behaves as traced.
severityWhy: At IBKR (margin account, 3x ETFs) it can leave an unwanted short of the algo's full size: a wrong position and real money at risk. The stale-stop path needs no second coincidence once you have sold by hand. You do get a push that positions differ within about 2 minutes, but it doesn't say the backup stop is still there. No exposure today because both algos are paper. The Webull member alone would be LOW, if Webull refuses sells beyond holdings.
plainTitle: Selling the algo's shares yourself can leave you short at IBKR
plainWhat: If you sell the live IBKR algo's shares yourself, in the IBKR app or from the board, the algo doesn't notice for 1-2 minutes and can sell the same shares again. Its backup stop order also stays at IBKR for shares you no longer own, and can sell later. Either one can leave you short a 3x fund. It can't happen while the algos are on paper, and Webull will most likely refuse the extra sells.
fix: Before every closing order (_exit/_live), read _broker_shares(). If it is None, wait. If it is 0, mark the record flat. If it is fewer than the ledger, cut the order down to it. When the position check finds the broker holds less than the ledger, cancel or resize the backup stop at once and say so in the push.
fixRisk:
- The broker position can lag a fill, and reads None or empty while IB Gateway is disconnected. It must be treated as unknown, never as 0 (see paper_trader.py:70-73).
- The fix must not break partial-fill booking, the SELL ALL / kill-switch coordination, the backup-stop 'unknown'/'gone' logic, or Auto-Hedge.

whatIsTrue:
Both members are correct.
1. Exit rules don't check the broker. A stop-loss, take-profit, exit rule or trailing stop sends the ledger's full share count without asking the broker. Only the Stop button checks. So an algo exit that fires up to about 60 s after a hand sale in the broker app always goes out, one at 60-120 s sometimes does, and after about 120 s safe mode blocks it.
2. The backup stop is never resized. It stays at the broker for the ledger's count, because step 3 compares it with the ledger only. It stays until one of these happens:
   - the algo's own stop-loss or exit rule fires in a session turned on for live (the A1 path cancels it, then the sell is blocked);
   - Alex presses Stop (it books the position flat and cancels the stop);
   - Alex uses live-reset and starts the algo again.
   An algo restart in this state refuses to start and leaves the GTC stop at IBKR with nothing watching it.
3. IBKR: a SELL on a margin account for shares not held becomes a short sale, so either path can leave Alex short a 3x ETF (up to the $25k cap).
4. Webull: closing sells use side SELL, and short sales use a separate SHORT side, so Webull most likely rejects the extra sell rather than opening a short (not verified against real Webull). Webull may also refuse a hand sale while the GTC stop holds the shares. Webull impact is therefore mostly a rejected order and noise, about MEDIUM, as reviewer B rated it.
5. Paper mode today is unaffected: paper places no broker orders, and a hand sale doesn't touch the paper record.
trigger:
Today (both algos paper): never.
After Go Live at IBKR, the trigger is Alex selling some or all of the algo's position in the IBKR app instead of the board's Stop or SELL ALL buttons. That is natural for a phone-first trader away from the Mac. Then either:
(a) The algo's own exit fires within about 1-2 min. This is likely to coincide, not chance: he sells into the same sharp drop that trips the 2% stop or trailing stop, or he sells at 9:29 just before overnight_gap's 9:30 exit. Either way the algo sells the same shares again and he is short.
(b) The stale GTC backup stop (IBKR: 4 am-8 pm) is hit before the algo's own stop-loss or exit rule cancels it. That happens when the price gaps through it (4 am or 9:30 open, a fast 1-minute fall in a 3x ETF), when the session is not turned on for live, or when the algo is stopped or restarted.
The chance per hand sale is roughly 5-20% for (a). For (b) it is meaningful whenever Alex doesn't press Stop afterwards.
Webull: same code path, but the broker most likely refuses the extra sell.
plainTitle: Selling the algo's shares yourself in the IBKR app can leave you short
plainWhat: If you sell the algo's shares yourself in the IBKR app (not with the board's Stop or SELL ALL buttons), the algo takes 1-2 minutes to notice. If its own sell rule fires in that time, it sells the same shares again, and IBKR turns that into a short position. Its backup stop order also stays at IBKR for shares you no longer own, and can later sell them short too. This only matters once you Go Live; paper trading isn't affected, and pressing the board's Stop button after a hand sale clears it.
fixRisk:
If the broker read failing (None) blocked exits, it would switch off stop-losses during IBKR reconnects or Webull HTTP errors, so None must fall back to sending.

The broker's position count lags for a moment after the algo's own fills. A single read could cancel a fresh backup stop or wrongly mark the position flat, so it needs two reads or a short grace period after fills.

Webull adds an HTTP call per exit, which can hit rate limits and runs under the 2 s timer lock.

After a partial hand sale, the remaining shares have no broker stop while safe mode lasts, because step 4 skips placing one in safe mode. Consider placing a stop sized to the broker's count.

Fake brokers in tests/algo-stress-test.py and tests/fake-brokers must report positions, or exits get clamped to 0 shares.

It must not double-book an exit when the backup stop itself sold the missing shares (the step-1 'unknown' path).

whatIsTrue:
The finding holds as stated.

An IBKR order still working when IB Gateway disconnects is always reported "unconfirmed", even when IBKR did answer:
- ib_async clears its order list on disconnect.
- The algo's watchdog keeps listening to the old order object, so IBKR's later status is thrown away ("No order found").
- The pause text then wrongly says "IBKR gave no final answer".

Webull reaches the same state when its API gives no answer for about 30 s after the cancel.

From then on:
- `pending` is never cleared, so the stop-loss, take-profit, exit rule, trailing stop and Stop button do nothing.
- No backup stop is placed. For an exit, the old one was already cancelled; for an entry that filled, there never was one.
- The once-a-minute position check is skipped, so its "positions differ" push can't fire.
- The connection-lost safe mode never clears.
- Nothing is pushed by the algo, and the guardian is silent too, because the process is alive and its heartbeat is fresh.
- The pause text tells a Go Live user to press Ctrl+C and run ./jb live.

One correction to C7: it is not true that only the Go Live card shows the pause. The algo tab shows a red "LIVE TRADING PAUSED" banner (algo.html:397-399), and the phone page's LIVE banner and the tab badges show "· PAUSED" through livectl.summary 'halted' (golive-ui.js:167, gateway.py:447). Those only help if Alex opens the page; no push and no widget shows it.
severityWhy: When it happens with real money, every safety switches off silently: stop-loss, trailing stop, backup stop at the broker, Stop button and the position check. The shares are left with nothing protecting them, or the account holds shares the algo doesn't know about, and no push goes out. That matches the "safety turns off silently / can lose real money" definition. It only applies after Go Live and the trigger is rare.
plainTitle: After a connection blip mid-order, live algo stops protecting your shares and never tells you
plainWhat: If the connection to IBKR or Webull hiccups while the live algo is selling or buying, the algo pauses itself, and the pause turns off its stop-loss, its backup stop at the broker and the Stop button. Your phone gets no alert, and the board still thinks the algo is healthy. The shares can keep falling with nothing protecting them until you happen to open the algo tab or the phone page. This only matters once you press Go Live; paper trading can't hit it.
fix: In core_trader unconfirmed() (and the guardian, when live_status 'halted' is set), send a loud push right away and repeat it while still paused, with Go Live wording. Then, after a reconnect, look the order up at the broker by orderId/permId (IBKR) or client_order_id (Webull) plus the real position, and settle `pending` from that answer.
fixRisk: Adding the push is safe. Clearing `pending` on its own, or putting a backup stop back while the in-doubt sell may still be working, could sell twice and leave the account short. Any auto-resolve must first check the broker's open orders and position. It needs testing against both reconnect cases (cancel reached the broker / cancel could not be sent, as in drive.py short and long) and a Webull API outage (wb_unconfirmed.py).

alsoNoticed.title: Backup stop placed and cancelled every few seconds after an unfilled exit when cancel_after_s < 30
alsoNoticed.detail: After an exit goes unfilled, _bstop_tick step 4 (core_trader.py:808) places a backup stop at once. The next trailing or stop-loss hit cancels it and waits (_exit, 520-528). The re-sent exit is then blocked by the 30 s duplicate guard (_guardian_block 921, 932), and step 4 places a new stop again. In the control run (drive.py control, fakelogs events at +22 to +30 s) this placed and cancelled three STP orders in about 8 s before the exit could go out again. It only happens when cancel_after_s is under 30 (allowed down to 5); with the default 60 the duplicate window has already passed.
